gaps.sentence: The author, about ___ there has been much debate, will speak at the festival.
gaps.hint: debate about the author — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: 'About whom' is required after the preposition 'about' when referring to a person.

gaps.sentence: The hotel, ___ rates include breakfast, is fully booked for the conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' marks possession even for things: the hotel whose rates…

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.
'What caused the fire' means 'the thing that caused it'; 'that' cannot act as the subject of this nominal clause.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: The shower suddenly stopped working, ___ meant we had to call a plumber.
gaps.hint: refers back to the whole event
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause after a comma.

gaps.sentence: She told me ___ had happened, but I didn't believe her.
gaps.explanation: 'What had happened' means 'the things that had happened'; 'that' cannot stand alone as the subject here.
